docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The BIG Library is a personal software development project designed to simulate a real-world library management system.

The project was created to strengthen programming skills in Python, practice Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), and gain hands-on experience with software design, testing, and technical documentation.

The application follows a modular architecture and is being developed with a strong focus on code quality, maintainability, and scalability.

docs.title: Project Goals
docs.text:
The main goals of this project are:

  • Practice Python development in a real application
  • Apply Object-Oriented Programming principles
  • Design maintainable and scalable software components
  • Develop automated tests
  • Improve software documentation skills
  • Explore modern development practices and tools

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
The application supports core library management operations, including:

  • Book management
  • User management
  • Loan management
  • Search capabilities
  • Data persistence
  • Input validation
  • Error handling

Additional functionality is planned as the project evolves.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
Current technologies used in the project include:

  • Python
  • Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
  • Git
  • GitHub
  • MkDocs
  • Markdown

Planned future technologies include:

  • SQL Database
  • FastAPI
  • Docker
  • CI/CD Pipelines

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
This project serves as a learning platform for:

  • Software architecture
  • Clean code principles
  • Automated testing
  • Documentation as Code (Docs-as-Code)
  • Version control with Git
  • GitHub workflows
  • API development

docs.title: Documentation Structure
docs.text:
The documentation is organized into several sections:

  • Overview
  • Requirements
  • Architecture
  • Data Model
  • Project Structure
  • Testing
  • Future Development

Each section describes a specific aspect of the system and its development process.

docs.title: Project Approach
docs.text:
The BIG Library is developed using an iterative approach.

New features are designed, implemented, tested, and documented as part of a continuous learning process.

The project combines software development practices with a quality-focused mindset inspired by professional testing and engineering environments.

docs.title: AI-Assisted Development
docs.text:
The project is supported by Microsoft Copilot, which is used as a development assistant and code reviewer.

Copilot helps with:

  • Code reviews
  • Refactoring suggestions
  • Technical decision support
  • Documentation improvements
  • Learning new concepts and technologies

The objective is to use AI responsibly as a productivity and learning tool while maintaining a solid understanding of the underlying implementation.

docs.title: Future Vision
docs.text:
The long-term goal is to evolve The BIG Library from a learning application into a more complete production-style solution.

Planned enhancements include:

  • SQL database integration
  • REST API development
  • User authentication and authorization
  • Docker deployment
  • CI/CD automation
  • Recommendation features
  • Expanded test coverage

These improvements will provide opportunities to gain practical experience across software development, testing, and modern application architecture.

docs.title: Repository
docs.text:
Source code and documentation are maintained in a GitHub repository and updated continuously as the project evolves.

This project is intended as both a technical learning journey and a practical demonstration of software engineering, testing, and documentation skills.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The BIG Library is a modular library management application developed in Python.

The project follows a layered architecture to separate responsibilities and improve maintainability, readability, and testability of the codebase.

The application is organized into independent modules responsible for business logic, data management, and user interactions.

docs.title: Architecture Principles
docs.text:
The project is based on the following principles:

  • Separation of concerns
  • Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
  • Modular design
  • Maintainable code
  • Testable code
  • Clear responsibility ownership

docs.text:
User

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Models represent the core business entities of the application.

Examples:

  • Book
  • User
  • Loan

Responsibilities:

  • store business data
  • define entity attributes
  • support business operations

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Services contain the business logic of the application.

Examples:

  • BookService
  • UserService
  • LoanService

Responsibilities:

  • process user requests
  • validate business rules
  • coordinate interactions between components

docs.title: Database Layer
docs.text:
The database layer is responsible for data persistence.

Responsibilities:

  • save data
  • load data
  • manage storage operations

The layer is isolated from business logic to simplify future database migrations and support scalability.

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
Utility modules provide reusable helper functions.

Examples:

  • logging
  • validation
  • configuration handling
  • data formatting

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
The project includes automated tests designed to validate business logic, verify expected behaviour, and support regression testing.

The testing approach reflects software testing practices used in real-world projects and helps ensure application quality as the codebase grows.

docs.title: Why Python?
docs.text: Python was selected because of its readability, extensive ecosystem, and suitability for learning software design and application development.

docs.title: Why OOP?
docs.text: Object-Oriented Programming enables better organization of business entities and supports scalability as the project grows.

docs.title: Why Layered Architecture?

docs.title: Future Architecture Improvements
docs.text:
The current architecture was intentionally designed to support future enhancements.

Planned areas of development include:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The data model defines the core entities used by The BIG Library and describes how they interact with each other.

The model is designed to support library operations such as book management, user management, and loan processing while maintaining simplicity, readability, and scalability.

docs.title: Core Entities
docs.text:
The application is based on three primary entities:

  • Book
  • User
  • Loan

These entities represent the core business objects of the system.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Book entity represents a library item that can be searched, borrowed, and returned.

docs.title: Main Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Description book_id Unique identifier title Book title author Book author category Book category publication_year Year of publication isbn International Standard Book Number availability_status Indicates whether the book is available

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
The Book entity is responsible for:

  • Storing book information
  • Providing book metadata
  • Supporting search operations
  • Supporting borrowing workflows

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The User entity represents a library member who can borrow books and manage borrowing activity.

docs.title: Main Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Description user_id Unique identifier first_name User first name last_name User last name email Contact email registration_date Date of registration active_status User account status

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
The User entity is responsible for:

  • Storing member information
  • Supporting loan operations
  • Tracking borrowing activity

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Loan entity represents the borrowing transaction between a user and a book.

docs.title: Main Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Description loan_id Unique identifier book_id Borrowed book reference user_id Borrowing user reference borrow_date Date of borrowing due_date Expected return date return_date Actual return date status Active or completed

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
The Loan entity is responsible for:

  • Tracking active loans
  • Tracking completed loans
  • Supporting availability checks
  • Maintaining borrowing history

docs.title: Conceptual Relationship Model
docs.text:
User
 │
 │ 1
 │
 ▼
Loan
 ▲
 │
 │ N
 │
Book

docs.title: User → Loan
docs.text:
A user may have multiple loans during the lifetime of the account.

Examples:

  • One user can borrow multiple books.
  • One user can have multiple historical loan records.

docs.title: Book → Loan
docs.text:
A book can appear in many loan records over time.

Examples:

  • A book may be borrowed by different users.
  • Historical borrowing activity is maintained.

docs.title: Loan → User
docs.text: Each loan belongs to exactly one user.

docs.title: Loan → Book
docs.text: Each loan is associated with exactly one book.

docs.title: Book Availability
docs.text:
A book can only be borrowed when:

availability_status = Available

If the book is already borrowed, the borrowing request must be rejected.

docs.title: Active Loan Constraint
docs.text:
A loan may only be active when:

  • A valid user exists
  • A valid book exists
  • The book is available

docs.title: Return Processing
docs.text:
When a book is returned:

  • Loan status changes to Completed
  • Return date is recorded
  • Book becomes available again

docs.title: Book Validation
docs.text:
The system validates:

  • Required fields
  • Valid publication year
  • Duplicate records
  • ISBN format

docs.title: User Validation
docs.text:
The system validates:

  • Required fields
  • Email format
  • Duplicate accounts

docs.title: Loan Validation
docs.text:
The system validates:

  • Existing user reference
  • Existing book reference
  • Book availability
  • Loan status consistency

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document describes the functional and non-functional requirements for The BIG Library.

The requirements define the expected behaviour of the system and provide a foundation for implementation, testing, and future enhancements.

docs.title: System Scope
docs.text:
The BIG Library is a library management application that enables users to manage books, library members, and lending operations.

The system focuses on supporting core library processes while providing a maintainable and scalable architecture.

docs.title: FR-001 Add Book
docs.text: The system shall allow a user to add a new book to the library catalogue.

docs.title: FR-002 View Book Details
docs.text: The system shall allow a user to view information about a selected book.

docs.title: FR-003 Search Books
docs.text: The system shall allow a user to search for books using defined criteria.

docs.title: FR-004 Update Book Information
docs.text: The system shall allow a user to update information about an existing book.

docs.title: FR-005 Remove Book
docs.text: The system shall allow a user to remove a book from the catalogue.

docs.title: FR-006 Prevent Duplicate Books
docs.text: The system shall prevent duplicate book records based on defined validation rules.

docs.title: FR-007 Register User
docs.text: The system shall allow a new library user to be registered.

docs.title: FR-008 View User Information
docs.text: The system shall allow viewing details of a registered user.

docs.title: FR-009 Update User Information
docs.text: The system shall allow modification of existing user information.

docs.title: FR-010 Remove User
docs.text: The system shall allow removal of a user from the system.

docs.title: FR-011 Prevent Duplicate Users
docs.text: The system shall prevent creation of duplicate user records.

docs.title: FR-012 Borrow Book
docs.text: The system shall allow a user to borrow an available book.

docs.title: FR-013 Return Book
docs.text: The system shall allow a borrowed book to be returned.

docs.title: FR-014 Track Active Loans
docs.text: The system shall maintain information about active loans.

docs.title: FR-015 Prevent Borrowing Unavailable Books
docs.text: The system shall prevent borrowing books that are already loaned out.

docs.title: FR-016 View Loan History
docs.text: The system shall provide access to historical loan records.

docs.title: FR-017 Mandatory Fields Validation
docs.text: The system shall validate that required fields are completed.

docs.title: FR-018 Invalid Input Validation
docs.text: The system shall reject invalid user input.

docs.title: FR-019 Business Rule Validation
docs.text: The system shall verify that all business rules are satisfied before processing requests.

docs.title: FR-020 Save Data
docs.text: The system shall support data persistence.

docs.title: FR-021 Load Data
docs.text: The system shall allow previously stored data to be loaded.

docs.title: FR-022 Maintain Data Integrity
docs.text: The system shall ensure consistency of stored information.

docs.title: NFR-001 Maintainability
docs.text: The application shall be implemented using a modular architecture to simplify maintenance and future development.

docs.title: NFR-002 Scalability
docs.text: The architecture shall support future enhancements without major redesign.

docs.title: NFR-003 Testability
docs.text: Application components shall be designed to support automated testing.

docs.title: NFR-004 Reliability
docs.text: The application shall handle expected errors without unexpected termination.

docs.title: NFR-005 Usability
docs.text: The application shall provide clear messages and predictable behaviour.

docs.title: Future Requirements
docs.text: The following requirements are planned for future releases.

docs.title: FR-023 User Authentication
docs.text: The system shall allow users to authenticate using credentials.

docs.title: FR-024 Reservation Management
docs.text: The system shall allow users to reserve books.

docs.title: FR-025 REST API
docs.text: The system shall expose selected functionality through REST endpoints.

docs.title: FR-026 Recommendation Engine
docs.text: The system shall provide book recommendations based on user activity.

docs.title: FR-027 Container Deployment
docs.text: The system shall support deployment using Docker.

docs.title: Requirement Traceability
docs.text:
The requirements defined in this document provide the basis for:

  • Solution design
  • Architecture decisions
  • Test scenarios
  • Automated tests
  • Future development planning

Each implemented feature should be traceable to one or more documented requirements.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Testing is a core part of The BIG Library project.

The goal of testing is to verify that business requirements are implemented correctly, application behaviour remains predictable, and future changes do not introduce regressions.

The testing approach combines development and quality assurance practices to promote reliability, maintainability, and confidence in the solution.

docs.title: Testing Objectives
docs.text:
The project aims to verify:

  • Functional correctness
  • Business rule validation
  • Data integrity
  • Input validation
  • Error handling
  • Edge case behaviour
  • Regression prevention

docs.title: Testing Scope
docs.text: The following areas are covered by testing activities:

docs.title: Book Management
docs.text:
• Add a book
  • Update book details
  • Remove a book
  • Search for books
  • Validate duplicate records

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
• Create a user
  • Update user information
  • Remove a user
  • Validate user data

docs.title: Loan Management
docs.text:
• Borrow a book
  • Return a book
  • Prevent borrowing unavailable books
  • Validate loan status changes

docs.title: Unit Testing
docs.text:
Unit tests validate individual components independently from the rest of the application.

Examples:

  • Book creation
  • User creation
  • Loan creation
  • Validation logic
  • Service methods

Benefits:

  • Early defect detection
  • Faster troubleshooting
  • Improved code quality

docs.title: Integration Testing
docs.text:
Integration testing validates interactions between multiple components.

Examples:

  • Services communicating with the database layer
  • Data persistence operations
  • Loan processing workflows
  • Data retrieval and updates

Benefits:

  • Verifies component collaboration
  • Detects interface issues
  • Confirms data consistency

docs.title: Add a New Book
docs.text:
Given

A valid book record

When

The user adds the book to the library

Then

The book should be successfully stored and visible in the catalogue

docs.title: Borrow a Book
docs.text:
Given

An available book exists in the library

When

A user borrows the book

Then

A loan record should be created and the book should no longer be available

docs.title: Return a Book
docs.text:
Given

An active loan exists

When

The user returns the book

Then

The loan should be closed and the book should become available again

docs.title: Search for a Book
docs.text:
Given

Books exist in the catalogue

When

The user searches using valid criteria

Then

Matching books should be returned

docs.title: Validation Testing
docs.text:
Validation testing ensures that incorrect inputs are handled properly.

Examples:

  • Missing mandatory fields
  • Empty values
  • Duplicate records
  • Invalid identifiers
  • Unsupported operations

Expected behaviour:

  • Validation errors should be displayed clearly
  • Invalid data should not be stored

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
Special attention is given to boundary and exceptional scenarios.

Examples:

  • Empty library catalogue
  • Empty user database
  • Duplicate books
  • Duplicate users
  • Borrowing already borrowed books
  • Returning books that are not currently borrowed
  • Deleting non-existing records

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The application should handle errors consistently and predictably.

Examples:

  • Missing records
  • Invalid user actions
  • Data access failures
  • Unexpected runtime errors

Expected behaviour:

  • Meaningful error messages
  • No application crashes
  • Data integrity maintained

docs.title: Automated Testing
docs.text:
Automated tests are used to validate key business logic and reduce manual verification effort.

Benefits include:

  • Faster feedback
  • Regression protection
  • Improved reliability
  • Easier refactoring

Automated tests are executed during development whenever new functionality is introduced or existing functionality is modified.

docs.title: Quality Assurance Approach
docs.text:
The project applies quality-focused development practices:

  • Requirements review
  • Code review
  • Test design
  • Automated testing
  • Defect investigation
  • Continuous improvement

This approach reflects software testing practices used in professional projects and supports long-term maintainability.

docs.title: Future Improvements
docs.text:
Planned testing enhancements include:

  • Increased test coverage
  • Test reporting
  • CI/CD integration
  • Performance testing
  • API testing after FastAPI implementation
  • Automated quality gates

docs.title: Quality Focus
docs.text:
Testing is treated as an integral part of development rather than a separate activity.

The objective is to build a reliable, maintainable, and scalable application while continuously improving both development and testing practices.
